meta.title: Jad Madi's OpenCode plugins
meta.description: Every OpenCode V2 plugin and skills pack, with what it is, what it solves, and where it lives.
meta.note: Entries with "published": false are private repos. A public site should skip them, or link them only where the reader has access.
meta.installNote: installCommand is the Git distribution path. This machine already has these plugins installed by copy or symlink, so do not run both or the plugin loads twice.
meta.versioning: CalVer YYYY.MM.MICRO (year.month.release counter; micro starts at 0), for example 2026.9.0.

plugins.name: model-switcher
plugins.title: Model Switcher
plugins.summary: Slash commands that switch provider and model mid-session, resolved against the live model catalog.
plugins.problem: Mid-session model choice is manual: you need the exact provider and model id, and there is no quick view of what fits an intent such as free, cheap, fast, or vision.

commands.name: /model
commands.description: Show the current model and switch by reference or group.

commands.name: /free
commands.description: Cycle models that cost nothing.

commands.name: /cheap
commands.description: Cycle paid models, cheapest first.

commands.name: /think
commands.description: Cycle reasoning models.

commands.name: /vision
commands.description: Cycle models that accept images.

commands.name: /long
commands.description: Cycle models with a 400k+ context window.

commands.name: /newest
commands.description: Cycle the newest models.

commands.name: /muse
commands.description: Cycle Muse models.

commands.name: /glm
commands.description: Cycle GLM models.

commands.name: /nvid
commands.description: Cycle NVIDIA models.

plugins.limits: The command set and pins come from ~/.config/opencode/model-switcher.json. No model ids are hard-coded.
plugins.install: Copy model-switcher.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: context-limit
plugins.title: Context Limit
plugins.summary: Sets a per-model working context budget by lowering the model window, so compaction fires before quality drops.
plugins.problem: A model's advertised window is larger than its useful working window, and one global compaction threshold is either too late for small models or too eager for large ones.

commands.name: /context-limit
commands.description: Show or set a working context budget for a model or pattern.

plugins.limits: It can only lower a model window, never raise it.
plugins.install: Copy context-limit.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: max-mode
plugins.title: Max Mode
plugins.summary: Runs 2 to 8 candidate answers in parallel for a hard question and returns the one a judge picks.
plugins.problem: Hard prompts benefit from several attempts, but generating them one at a time and comparing them by hand is slow and hides the reasoning.

commands.name: /max
commands.description: Set the default best-of-N candidate count for the session.

plugins.limits: Cost multiplies with the candidate count. It calls ctx.generate.text, so set MAX_MODE_MODEL on providers that reject transient generation.
plugins.install: Copy max-mode.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: memory
plugins.title: Memory
plugins.summary: Keeps per-project memory, checkpoints, and notes, injects a budgeted slice at session start, and exposes read, append, and search tools.
plugins.problem: Sessions and compaction lose context; decisions, file state, and next steps need a durable project store that survives both.

commands.name: /remember
commands.description: Append a line to MEMORY.md.

commands.name: /memory
commands.description: Show the three memory files.

commands.name: /checkpoint
commands.description: Write a memory checkpoint now.

plugins.limits: Files live under the OpenCode data dir per project. MEMORY_ROOT and MEMORY_BUDGET override location and size. A checkpoint is written on compaction.
plugins.install: Copy memory.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: sila
plugins.title: Sila Sidebar
plugins.summary: Puts sila goals, the bound goal and its tasks, and open handoff items in the TUI sidebar, with commands to focus, claim, release, report, open, and toggle tasks.
plugins.problem: Goal and task state lives in the sila store, out of sight while you work, and acting on it means leaving the TUI for the shell.

commands.name: /sila-focus
commands.description: Bind this session to a goal and claim it when free.

commands.name: /sila-open
commands.description: Open the bound goal's goal.md with $SILA_EDITOR.

commands.name: /sila-claim
commands.description: Claim the bound goal for this session.

commands.name: /sila-release
commands.description: Release the bound goal when this agent holds it.

commands.name: /sila-report
commands.description: Record a progress note on the bound goal.

commands.name: /sila-task
commands.description: Toggle a numbered task on the bound goal.

plugins.limits: Read-only except explicit actions. Release refuses another agent's claim, and one session binds to one goal per repo. Env: SILA_BIN, SILA_POLL_MS, SILA_MAX_GOALS, SILA_MAX_TASKS, SILA_EDITOR.
plugins.install: Symlink the repo into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-sila (the repo's script/install does this).

plugins.name: sila-prime
plugins.title: Sila Prime
plugins.summary: Runs sila prime on the first prompt and injects the cross-tool briefing, plus a /sila command for any sila subcommand.
plugins.problem: Each session starts without the sila knowledge store unless you remember to run the CLI first.

commands.name: /sila
commands.description: Run a sila subcommand and post the output (default: prime).

plugins.limits: Calls the sila CLI. SILA_BIN points at the binary, SILA_PRIME=off disables the briefing, and SILA_PRIME_BUDGET caps it. The session is marked after one attempt, so /sila refreshes on demand.
plugins.install: Copy sila-prime.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: task-tool
plugins.title: Task Tool
plugins.summary: A tree task tool with stable T1, T1.1 ids that survive long turns and compaction.
plugins.problem: Multi-step work loses its structure in long sessions, and ad hoc lists renumber or disappear when the context compacts.
plugins.limits: State is per session and ids never renumber.
plugins.install: Copy task-tool.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: goal
plugins.title: Goal
plugins.summary: Sets a judged stopping condition per session: at turn end a separate judge decides whether the goal is met, and the plugin continues with a nudge or gives up at a cap.
plugins.problem: An agent decides it is done on its own, so a stopping condition needs an independent check to avoid ending early or running away.

commands.name: /goal
commands.description: Set, show, or clear the judged stopping condition for this session.

plugins.limits: It calls ctx.generate.text, so set GOAL_MODEL on providers that reject transient generation. Continuations are capped by GOAL_MAX (default 5).
plugins.install: Copy goal.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: workflows
plugins.title: Workflows
plugins.summary: Runs deterministic multi-agent workflows with resumable artifacts. Ships deep-research from brief to review.
plugins.problem: Multi-phase work such as research is repeated ad hoc, with no fixed order, no artifacts, and no way to resume a run.

commands.name: /workflow
commands.description: Run a workflow by name, or list the available workflows.

plugins.limits: Uses child sessions and inherits the invoking session's model, so it needs no override. Runs are resumable from artifacts under the data dir.
plugins.install: Copy workflows.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: loop
plugins.title: Loop
plugins.summary: Runs a prompt on a fixed cadence, skipping a tick while the previous run is still active.
plugins.problem: Recurring checks need a timer, but naive timers fire while the last run is still going and pile work up.

commands.name: /loop
commands.description: Register, list, or stop a recurring prompt on a fixed cadence.

plugins.limits: One loop per session, because the turn-end event names the session, not the run.
plugins.install: Copy loop.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: compose-next
plugins.title: Compose Next
plugins.summary: A spec-to-ship workflow as a skill: grill, spec, workspace, implement, verify, review, finalize, finish, with a read-only reviewer.
plugins.problem: Work that jumps straight to code skips design and review; the path from idea to a merged change needs a repeatable order and an independent reviewer.

commands.name: /compose-next
commands.description: Start the spec-to-ship workflow and attach the compose-next skill.

plugins.limits: Needs the compose-next skill installed under ~/.config/opencode/skills/compose-next/SKILL.md.
plugins.install: Copy compose-next.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and the skill into ~/.config/opencode/skills/.

plugins.name: skip-permissions
plugins.title: Skip Permissions
plugins.summary: Upgrades permission ask decisions to allow for one session through a permission hook.
plugins.problem: Approval prompts interrupt trusted work in a session you already control, adding friction without adding safety.

commands.name: /skip-permissions
commands.description: Toggle auto-approval of ask decisions for this session, or show the state.

plugins.limits: It only upgrades an ask to an allow. A configured deny is final and never reaches the hook.
plugins.install: Copy skip-permissions.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: distill
plugins.title: Distill
plugins.summary: Finds repeated multi-step workflows in session history and proposes a skill, command, or subagent for them.
plugins.problem: The same procedure gets repeated by hand instead of becoming a reusable artifact, and nothing should be written until you apply it.

commands.name: /distill
commands.description: Propose reusable artifacts from session history, list proposals, or apply one.

plugins.limits: Writes only on an explicit /distill apply and never overwrites an existing artifact. It calls ctx.generate.text, so set DISTILL_MODEL on providers that reject transient generation.
plugins.install: Copy distill.ts into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and restart the TUI.

plugins.name: data-analytics
plugins.title: Data Analytics Skills
plugins.summary: Six data-analysis skills that load by intent: data quality, KPI design, metric diagnostics, product and business analysis, validation, and visualization.
plugins.problem: Analytics work repeats the same validation, KPI, diagnostics, and charting steps without a shared, reusable procedure.
plugins.limits: A skills pack, not a plugin. It ships six skills: da-analyze-data-quality, da-design-kpis, da-metric-diagnostics, da-product-biz-analysis, da-validate-data, da-visualize-data.
plugins.install: Copy the skills/ directory into ~/.config/opencode/skills/ (or .opencode/skills/ for one project).
